description: Modern statistical modelling for data that is clustered, censored, multivariate, sequential or high dimensional, covering generalised, mixed, Bayesian, survival and state-space models. Students fit and diagnose models in code, derive key estimators and finish with an analysis of a public-health or agricultural dataset.
modelledOn: Gelman, Hill and Vehtari, Regression and Other Stories
McCullagh and Nelder, Generalized Linear Models
Wood, Generalized Additive Models: An Introduction with R
Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice
outcomes: Specify, fit and diagnose generalised linear and additive models for binary, count and skewed outcomes.
Build mixed-effects and hierarchical models for clustered and longitudinal data and interpret variance components and shrinkage.
Implement and check Bayesian inference with MCMC, including convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks.
Analyse censored time-to-event data with Kaplan-Meier, Cox and parametric models.
Apply multivariate methods, missing-data handling and state-space forecasting appropriately.
Validate models with resampling and calibration at scale and communicate uncertainty reproducibly.

units.title: Generalised linear and additive models
topics: Exponential family, link functions and fitting by iteratively reweighted least squares
Logistic, Poisson and negative binomial regression; overdispersion and zero inflation
Deviance, residuals, influence and model selection with AIC and BIC
Penalised regression: ridge, lasso and elastic net
Generalised additive models: splines, smoothing penalties and effective degrees of freedom

units.title: Mixed-effects and hierarchical models
topics: Random intercepts and slopes; variance components and the intraclass correlation
Estimation: maximum likelihood, REML and the Laplace approximation for generalised mixed models
Longitudinal data: repeated measures and correlation structures
Multilevel designs: patients within clinics within districts; crossed random effects
Shrinkage, best linear unbiased predictors and comparing mixed models

units.title: Bayesian modelling and MCMC
topics: Priors, conjugacy, posterior summaries and credible intervals
Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs sampling
Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and the No-U-Turn sampler; divergent transitions
Convergence diagnostics: trace plots, R-hat and effective sample size
Posterior predictive checks, WAIC and leave-one-out cross-validation
Hierarchical Bayesian models and partial pooling

units.title: Survival and event-history analysis
topics: Censoring, survival and hazard functions; the Kaplan-Meier estimator
The log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards with partial likelihood
Parametric survival: Weibull and accelerated failure time models
Time-varying covariates and competing risks
Frailty models and recurrent events

units.title: Multivariate methods and missing data
topics: Principal components and factor analysis
Canonical correlation and multivariate analysis of variance
Discriminant analysis and clustering: k-means, hierarchical and Gaussian mixtures with EM
Multidimensional scaling and distance-based methods
Missing data mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and multiple imputation
Dimension reduction for compositional and count data

units.title: State-space and forecasting models
topics: ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA: identification, estimation and diagnostics
State-space form, the Kalman filter and smoother
Exponential smoothing and structural time-series models
Dynamic regression and intervention analysis
Forecast evaluation: rolling origin, proper scoring rules and prediction intervals
Count time series for disease surveillance (weekly malaria and cholera counts)

units.title: Resampling and model validation at scale
topics: The bootstrap: percentile and bias-corrected intervals; bootstrapping dependent data
Cross-validation, leakage and nested validation
Calibration and proper scoring rules for probabilistic predictions
Large-scale multiple testing and permutation tests
Computation at scale: sparse matrices, subsampling and stochastic optimisation

units.title: Workflow, interpretation and project
topics: A model-building workflow: exploration, assumptions, fitting, diagnostics and revision
Predictive versus explanatory models: interpretation pitfalls
Reproducible reporting of models and uncertainty
Project: an end-to-end analysis of a health or agriculture dataset

schedule.title: Generalised linear models
schedule.exercise: Derive the IRLS update for logistic regression, fit it by hand for four observations and interpret the odds ratios of a malaria-test dataset with deviance residuals.

tasks.title: Compute two IRLS iterations for a logistic regression with four data points and check the coefficients against the closed-form likelihood gradient
Fit Poisson and negative binomial models to clinic visit counts, compare dispersion and choose between them with a residual check
Compare six candidate GLMs by AIC and BIC, plot Cook's distance and decide if the best model is supported by diagnostics

schedule.title: Penalisation and additive models
schedule.exercise: Compare ridge and lasso paths on a correlated predictor set and explain what a smoothing penalty does when fitting a spline to rainfall and maize yield.

tasks.title: Plot ridge and lasso coefficient paths against lambda on a 10-predictor dataset and say which variables the lasso drops first
Fit a spline smooth of yield on rainfall, vary the smoothing parameter and show the trade-off between wiggliness and effective degrees of freedom
Fit an additive model with two smooth terms and a factor, use cross-validation to pick penalties, and plot partial effects with intervals

schedule.title: Random effects and variance components
schedule.exercise: Model blood-pressure readings of patients nested in clinics with a random intercept, compute the intraclass correlation and interpret how much variation lies between clinics.

tasks.title: Compute the intraclass correlation from given between-clinic and within-clinic variances and the shrinkage factor for a clinic with 5 patients
Fit random intercept and random slope models to repeated visits and test whether the slope variance is needed using a likelihood ratio
Compare ML and REML variance estimates on a small clinic dataset by simulation and show the downward bias of ML

schedule.title: Longitudinal and multilevel structures
schedule.exercise: Analyse a trial where children are measured four times in schools within districts, choose a correlation structure and compare fixed-effect conclusions across three random structures.

tasks.title: Fit a repeated-measures model with compound symmetry and an autoregressive structure and pick one by AIC and residual correlation plots
Fit a three-level model for pupils in schools in districts, report variance at each level and say where an intervention should target
Plot raw group means against shrunken predictions for 20 clinics of varying size and explain why small clinics move more

schedule.title: Bayesian inference and sampling
schedule.exercise: Update a Beta prior for vaccine uptake with survey data, compare informative and flat priors, then implement Metropolis-Hastings for a two-parameter posterior.

tasks.title: Update a Beta(2,8) prior with 30 successes in 100 trials, plot prior, likelihood and posterior, and give a 95 percent credible interval
Code a random-walk Metropolis sampler for a logistic regression posterior and tune the proposal scale to reach about 25 percent acceptance
Implement a Gibbs sampler for a normal model with unknown mean and variance and verify it against the analytic posterior

schedule.title: Hamiltonian sampling, checking and hierarchies
schedule.exercise: Fit a hierarchical model of district-level immunisation rates, check chains, run a posterior predictive check and compare partial pooling with complete and no pooling.

tasks.title: Read trace plots, R-hat and effective sample size for four chains and decide which of three runs has not converged
Code a leapfrog Hamiltonian step on a 2D correlated Gaussian target and compare effective sample size per second with random-walk Metropolis
Fit eight-school-style hierarchical data with centred and non-centred parameterisations, count divergences and compare WAIC for pooled models

schedule.title: Survival analysis
schedule.exercise: Estimate survival curves of patients on two treatment pathways, compare them with a log-rank test and fit a Cox model with age and a time-varying covariate, checking proportional hazards.

tasks.title: Compute a Kaplan-Meier curve by hand for 12 censored follow-up times and read off the median survival and its meaning
Fit a Cox proportional hazards model to a HIV-care dataset, interpret hazard ratios and test proportional hazards with scaled Schoenfeld residuals
Fit Weibull and log-normal accelerated failure time models, compare with the Cox fit and predict survival at 12 months for two profiles

schedule.title: Principal components and discriminant methods
schedule.exercise: Reduce a 12-variable household-survey table with principal components, decide the number of components with a scree plot, then cluster households using a Gaussian mixture.

tasks.title: Compute the principal components of a 4-variable covariance matrix and the proportion of variance explained by each component
Fit k-means with k from 2 to 8 and a Gaussian mixture with EM and compare silhouette and BIC to select the number of groups
Carry out MANOVA on three crop-quality measures across fertiliser types and follow up with discriminant analysis on the significant contrasts

schedule.title: Distances, missing data and compositions
schedule.exercise: Create 30 percent missing values under MCAR and MAR in a health dataset, impute multiply and compare estimates and intervals with complete-case analysis.

tasks.title: Compute a classical multidimensional scaling map from a 5x5 distance table between regions and interpret the first two axes
Impose MAR missingness, run multiple imputation with 20 datasets, pool the results with the standard combining rules and compare bias against the complete-case estimate
Transform compositional soil-nutrient data with a log-ratio transform before PCA and show how the raw percentages mislead the correlation

schedule.title: ARIMA and state-space models
schedule.exercise: Identify and fit a seasonal ARIMA model to monthly electricity-demand data, write the same model in state-space form and run a Kalman filter on a local-level model.

tasks.title: Read ACF and PACF plots for three simulated series and propose an ARIMA order for each with a reason
Implement a Kalman filter for a local-level model, filter noisy sensor data and plot the estimated level with its 95 percent band
Fit exponential smoothing and a structural time-series model to monthly rainfall, then compare their forecasts for the next 12 months

schedule.title: Forecast evaluation and surveillance data
schedule.exercise: Build a weekly forecast for cholera cases with prediction intervals, evaluate it by rolling origin and report both point error and interval coverage.

tasks.title: Add an intervention term to a mobile-money transaction series for a fee change and estimate the size and decay of its effect
Evaluate three forecasting methods with rolling-origin cross-validation and compare their continuous ranked probability scores
Fit a negative binomial regression with seasonal terms to weekly case counts and forecast the next 8 weeks with intervals

schedule.title: Resampling, calibration and scale
schedule.exercise: Validate a clinical risk model with nested cross-validation and bootstrap, assess calibration with a reliability plot and a Brier score, and discuss a leakage that inflated an earlier result.

tasks.title: Bootstrap the median of a skewed income sample 2000 times and compare the percentile and bias-corrected intervals
Show data leakage by scaling before splitting, then repair the pipeline with nested cross-validation and report the honest error
Draw a calibration plot and compute the Brier score for a risk model, then recalibrate it with isotonic regression

schedule.title: Workflow and project
schedule.exercise: Present an end-to-end analysis of a maternal-health or crop-yield dataset: question, model choice, diagnostics, uncertainty, limitations and a reproducible report.

tasks.title: Run the full model-building workflow on a given dataset and record each diagnostic check, revision and the reason for it
Show on simulated data how a good predictive model can give a misleading causal reading of one coefficient
Produce a reproducible notebook for the project analysis that regenerates all tables and figures from raw data with one command
